intervention_window.observation_summary: The data reveals a consistent concentration spike during 07:00–10:00 on weekdays, with average values 37.4% higher than the remainder of the diurnal cycle, and an exceedance frequency of 47.5%.

insights.title: Dominant Driver
insights.headline: PM10 Dictated AQI in 54.0% of Observations
insights.detail: Across 7,320 station-day calculations, PM10 produced the highest sub-index 3,953 times, making it the primary target for exposure reduction.

insights.title: Exposure Exceedance
insights.headline: 37.4% of Observed Days Exceeded CPCB Poor Threshold
insights.detail: A total of 2737 days breached the 200 AQI mark, with the highest single-day station reading reaching 500.

insights.title: Seasonal Inversion Dynamic
insights.headline: Winter Pollution Averaged 2.9x Higher than Monsoon
insights.detail: Atmospheric dispersion during wet monsoon periods lowered average AQI to 94.4, compared to 273.4 during shallow winter boundary layer conditions.

insights.title: Combustion & Commuter Signature
insights.headline: NO2 Levels Rose 23.4% on Weekdays vs Weekends
insights.detail: Nitrogen dioxide concentrations averaged 46.1 µg/m³ during Monday–Friday commuter hours compared to 37.4 µg/m³ on weekends.

story_delhi.title: Atmospheric Baseline & Urban Exposure Briefing: Delhi
story_delhi.subtitle: An empirical forensic review of air quality telemetry, pollutant drivers, and exposure windows

situation.headline: Annual Mean AQI Stood at 297.5 Across 4 Monitored Stations
situation.narrative: Continuous ambient monitoring across Delhi recorded an average annual Air Quality Index of 297.5. Peak single-day degradation reached an AQI of 500. Active monitors in the network include Anand Vihar, Delhi, IGI Airport (T3), Delhi, Punjabi Bagh, Delhi and others.

driver.headline: PM2.5 Was the Governing Pollutant in 60.6% of All Assessments
driver.narrative: Air Quality Index values are governed by the highest individual pollutant sub-index. In Delhi, PM2.5 was the dominant sub-index driver in 60.6% of monitored days, indicating that fine particulate accumulation represents the immediate respiratory risk factor.

pattern.headline: Winter Concentrations Were 2.6x Higher than Monsoon Baselines
pattern.narrative: The atmospheric profile demonstrates strong seasonal contrast. Winter periods averaged an AQI of 405.9, compared to 154.2 during wet monsoon months. This indicates strong meteorological modulation where lower boundary layer heights trap local surface emissions.

exposure.headline: 1055 Days (72.1%) Breached the CPCB 'Poor' Threshold
exposure.narrative: Residents experienced 1055 days of air quality rated Poor or worse (AQI > 200). Of these, 325 days reached the Severe category (AQI > 400), necessitating emergency advisories.

intervention_window.headline: Critical Recurring Risk Window: 07:00–10:00 on Weekdays
intervention_window.narrative: Statistical aggregation identifies 07:00–10:00 on Weekdays as the primary recurring risk period. Ambient concentrations during this timeframe average 37.6% higher than the baseline diurnal cycle, with an exceedance frequency of 100.0%.
intervention_window.recommendation: Target traffic management, road dust suppression, and public exposure advisories specifically to this 3-hour window.
